message:
Initial commit with task details

Adding .gitkeep for PR creation (default mode).
This file will be removed when the task is complete.

Issue: https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/185
chore: remove .gitkeep added for PR creation

feat(js): default to Chrome for Testing without its infobar or keychain prompts (#179)

resolveLaunchExecutable() now prefers the engine's bundled Chrome for
Testing and never falls back to the user's Google Chrome unless
channel: 'chrome' or executablePath asks for it. A Chrome for Testing
executable gets the new chrome-for-testing restriction preset
(--test-type=gpu, --use-mock-keychain) by default; defaultRestrictions: []
opts out.

fix: capture trace and default screenshots without a clip (#180)

A clipped engine capture can leave a resized headful window drawn at its
old size. Trace checkpoint screenshots and default captures of a page
without a fixed viewport now use CDP Page.captureScreenshot with no clip,
in JS, Python and Rust.
refactor(js): share engine loaders and launch test setup

feat(js): selenium downloads Chrome for Testing rather than using Google Chrome (#179)

Without a Chrome for Testing of Playwright or Puppeteer, launchBrowser
asks Selenium Manager for --force-browser-download (new downloadBrowser
option of launchWebDriver and resolveWebDriverExecutable).
test(js): share the Selenium Manager fake in webdriver tests

fix(js): migrate passwords with the Chrome for Testing keychain key (#179)

A default launch now starts Chrome for Testing, which keeps its key under
"Chromium Safe Storage" and, with --use-mock-keychain, derives it from
Chromium's fixed mock password. Pre-launch migration now encrypts with the
key of the browser that actually starts. macOS keys are tagged v10, the only
prefix macOS Chromium reads.

feat(python): default to Chrome for Testing without its infobar or keychain prompts (#179)

Mirrors the JavaScript change: resolve_launch_executable starts Playwright's
Chrome for Testing unless channel/executable_path asks for another browser,
Chrome for Testing launches get the chrome-for-testing restrictions
(--test-type=gpu, --use-mock-keychain) unless default_restrictions is given,
Selenium is pointed at Chrome for Testing, and pre-launch migration encrypts
passwords with the key of the browser that starts.
fix(rust): migrate passwords with the Chrome for Testing keychain key (#179)

feat(rust): default to Chrome for Testing without its infobar or keychain prompts (#179)

Without channel or executable_path, launch_browser and launch_real_browser
start the Chrome for Testing that Playwright, Puppeteer or Selenium Manager
downloaded, never the installed Google Chrome, and fail with install hints
when there is none. A Chrome for Testing launch gets the chrome-for-testing
preset (--test-type=gpu, --use-mock-keychain) unless default_restrictions
replaces it; the result reports the defaults, parity counts them as
requested, and fantoccini pairs the download with its own chromedriver.
test: claim the launch.chrome-for-testing and trace.screenshots parity features (#179, #180)

chore(deps): take the rustls-webpki, launch-editor and markdown-it security fixes

RUSTSEC-2026-0382, GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv, GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw,
GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm, GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7, GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q and
GHSA-gfr2-rv44-r23c were published on 2026-10-20 and fail the Security
workflow on every branch.
style: lint the issue #179 and #180 experiment probes

fix(js): match ChromeDriver to the Chrome for Testing the session started (#179)

A real Selenium launch and a hand-off reattach resolved ChromeDriver without
the started browser's path, so Selenium Manager (or a chromedriver on PATH)
picked the driver of the installed Google Chrome and refused Chrome for
Testing. Pass the executable through and never use a PATH driver for Chrome
for Testing. Adds an e2e test that reads chrome://version for every engine
and measures the infobar the default restrictions hide.
refactor(js): keep the WebDriver and real-browser launch helpers within the complexity limit
refactor(js): keep the WebDriver and real-browser launch helpers within the complexity limit

fix(python): match ChromeDriver to the Chrome for Testing a real launch started (#179)

Selenium attached to a real launch with only a debugger address, so Selenium
Manager picked the driver of the installed Google Chrome. Give it the
started browser as binary_location.

ci: install every engine's Chrome for Testing and run its e2e suite (#179)

Launches without a channel now start Chrome for Testing, which
npm ci --ignore-scripts never downloads. Install it for Playwright and
Puppeteer in JavaScript and for Python's Playwright, verify each engine
resolves it, and run the Chrome for Testing e2e suite headfully.
docs: describe the Chrome for Testing default and its restrictions (#179)
chore: add release notes for Chrome for Testing defaults and unclipped screenshots (#179, #180)

fix(ci): pin rust-cache to its exact version and keep a timed-out 5xx link transient

zizmor's ref-version-mismatch failed the CI policy: Swatinem/rust-cache's v2
tag moved to v2.9.3 while safari.yml pins v2.9.2's commit, so the comment now
names that exact version. The link check failed two chromium.googlesource.com
links whose 503 was followed by a re-check timeout; neither answer said the
link is gone, so the verdict is transient.
ci: give Chrome for Testing a usable sandbox in the engine lifecycle suites (#179)
docs: explain Chrome for Testing's sandbox on Ubuntu 23.10 and newer (#179)

message:
fix(ci): accept links to files this branch adds

The READMEs link docs/chrome-for-testing.md on main, which 404s until this
pull request merges (run 39651456194). A 404 for a blob/tree/main link of
the repository itself whose file exists in the checkout is now reported as
a notice, not a broken link.

test: pin the startup-readiness and fantoccini driver tests to an explicit browser

Without a channel, a launch now starts Chrome for Testing, which the macOS
JS job and the Rust jobs do not install (runs 39651456004, 39651456107).
The startup regression is about the installed Google Chrome, so it asks for
channel 'chrome'; the fantoccini driver test only needs some executable so
the missing driver is what fails.

fix: skip a PATH chromedriver of another release for Chrome for Testing (#179)

Selenium Manager returns a chromedriver found on PATH even for a
--browser-path of another release, so Selenium refused Chrome for Testing
('This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version 155', run
39651456089). JS now passes --skip-driver-in-path when it downloads or
drives Chrome for Testing; Python resolves the driver that way and hands it
to Service for real and engine launches.

fix(rust): fantoccini prefers a Chrome for Testing it has the chromedriver of (#179)

A Playwright download has no chromedriver, so fantoccini fell back to the
one on PATH, which belongs to the installed Google Chrome. Take the first
cached release with its own chromedriver, else the first download, and
document the PATH fallback and Selenium's --skip-driver-in-path.

Merge main (PR #184) into issue-185: keep main's implementation of #179/#180

PR #184 landed a parallel implementation of #179, #180, #181 and #183.
This merge takes main's tree as is; the fixes this branch has that main
lacks follow as separate commits on top.

fix(ci): count a 5xx-then-timeout as transient, accept links to files this branch adds, pin the rust-cache comment

Ported from this branch's earlier commits onto main: the Broken Link
Checker treats a 5xx followed by a timeout as transient and a 404 to a
blob/main link of a file the checkout has as unmerged; the safari.yml
rust-cache comment names the exact tag so zizmor's ref-version-mismatch
stays quiet.

fix(js): Selenium matches Chrome for Testing with its own ChromeDriver (#179)

Main resolved ChromeDriver from PATH first and let Selenium Manager do the
same, so a chromedriver of the installed Google Chrome was paired with
Chrome for Testing and refused to start it. A Chrome for Testing
executable now skips PATH, Selenium Manager gets --skip-driver-in-path,
and the real-launch attach and the hand-off reattach pass the started
browser through. Also exports defaultRestrictionsFor().

fix(js): migrate passwords with Chrome for Testing's key and its mock keychain (#179)

Main kept targetBrowser: channel, so passwords migrated into a Chrome for
Testing launch (which runs with --use-mock-keychain by default) were
encrypted with Google Chrome's real Keychain key and could not be read.
The target is now 'chromium' for Chrome for Testing, targetKeystore
follows the launch switches, and macOS uses the v10 prefix.

test(e2e): every engine starts Chrome for Testing without its infobar or keychain (#179)

Ports this branch's end-to-end check onto main: Playwright, Puppeteer and
Selenium launches report a Chrome for Testing on chrome://version with
--test-type=gpu and --use-mock-keychain, and the opt-out shows the
infobar the defaults hide. Browser Parity installs every engine's Chrome
for Testing, verifies each is found, and lifts the AppArmor userns
restriction that leaves Chrome for Testing without a sandbox on
ubuntu-24.04.

fix(python): Selenium matches Chrome for Testing with its own ChromeDriver (#179)

Main gave Selenium a bare Service(), so Selenium Manager returned a
chromedriver on PATH of another release and the Chrome for Testing launch
failed with 'This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version
153' (experiments/issue-179/selenium-path-driver.py reproduces it with a
153 driver on PATH and a 156 Chrome for Testing). chrome_for_testing_driver()
asks Selenium Manager with --browser-path and --skip-driver-in-path for
the engine launch and the connector, and the real launch passes the
started browser as ConnectOptions.executable_path.

fix(python): migrate passwords with Chrome for Testing's key and its mock keychain (#179)

Main targeted options.channel or 'chrome', so a default launch - Chrome
for Testing with --use-mock-keychain - got passwords encrypted with
Google Chrome's real Keychain key. The target is now 'chromium' for
Chrome for Testing, the keystore follows the launch switches (mock for
--use-mock-keychain on macOS and --password-store=basic on Linux), and
macOS uses the v10 prefix.
fix(python): parity counts Chrome for Testing's default switches as requested (#179)
docs(python): changelog fragment heading
docs: Chrome for Testing by default, its ChromeDriver and the Ubuntu sandbox (#179)
chore(js): one changeset for the Chrome for Testing fixes (#179)

fix(rust): engine launches start Chrome for Testing and drive it with its own chromedriver (#179)

chromiumoxide's own detection started the installed Google Chrome, and
fantoccini used the chromedriver on PATH, which refuses another release.
experiments/rust-engine-before-main.txt shows both on main.
